slug.note: Cartridge identity, lowercase ASCII with hyphens, e.g. "308-winchester". This is the primary key and the join target for the pressure tables, so a slug change orphans every pressure figure that referenced it.

name.note: Full designation as published, e.g. ".308 Winchester".

short_name.note: Abbreviated form used in dense UI, e.g. "308 Win". Falls back to `name`.

family.note: Also the filename. family is NOT NULL in SQLite and a wrong guess files a pistol cartridge on a rifle page, so it is constrained rather than inferred.

parent_case.note: Case this cartridge is loaded on. EMPTY ON ALL 229 ROWS - not yet transcribed, and deliberately left empty rather than guessed.

bullet_dia_in.note: Nominal bullet diameter, inches. EMPTY ON ALL ROWS.

case_length_max_in.note: CIP/SAAMI maximum case length, inches. EMPTY ON ALL ROWS.

max_col_in.note: Overall cartridge length limit, inches. EMPTY ON ALL ROWS.

saami_max_psi.note: SAAMI maximum pressure, psi. The one dimension-like column that IS populated - all 229 rows carry a figure from the kwk.us compilation, with ksi rounded up to the nearest 1000 psi.

saami_max_cup.note: Maximum pressure in cup. Blank throughout.

cip_max_bar.note: CIP maximum pressure, bar. EMPTY ON ALL ROWS - CIP data is an open gap.

rim_dia_in.note: Rim diameter, inches. EMPTY ON ALL ROWS.

head_dia_in.note: Case head diameter, inches. EMPTY ON ALL ROWS.

capacity_gr_h2o.note: Case capacity in grains of water. EMPTY ON ALL ROWS.

primer_type.note: Smallest primer the case accepts, e.g. "small". EMPTY ON ALL ROWS.

typical_twist_in.note: Typical rifling twist rate, in per inch. EMPTY ON ALL ROWS.

is_reloadable.note: Whether the case is reloadable. The loader defaults to true when blank.

notes.note: Free prose. May contain commas, so it must stay quoted in the CSV.

source_name.note: Which publisher the row was read from. All 229 rows are "kwk.us Cartridge Pressure Standards" - one source for the whole dataset, which is why these are compilation figures rather than primary data.

source_note.note: How the value was derived, e.g. that ksi was rounded up.
